b.request: Treat every player in `appearances` that matches a `player` row as included, even if `player.death_country` is blank or NULL (such as living players). For each one, total `g_1b` − `g_cf` over their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep the players whose total is above the average of those totals, then return one row with the sum of their totals and the average amount by which those totals exceed the overall average, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT a.player_id, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total FROM appearances a WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM player p WHERE p.player_id = a.player_id) GROUP BY a.player_id), avg_t AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS av FROM t) SELECT SUM(t.total) AS sum_totals, AVG(t.total - avg_t.av) AS avg_excess FROM t, avg_t WHERE t.total > avg_t.av

c.request: For each player in `appearances` matched to `player`, together with the country they died in (`player.death_country`), total games at first base minus games in center field (`g_1b` − `g_cf`) across their appearance rows, skipping rows where either value is missing. Keep the players whose total is above the average total. Give a single row with two values: the sum of their totals, and the average amount by which they exceed that average. Don't round anything. All matched players count, including those with a blank death country (for example, living players).
c.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.player_id, p.death_country, SUM(a.g_1b - a.g_cf) AS total FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE a.g_1b IS NOT NULL AND a.g_cf IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.player_id, p.death_country), av AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM t) SELECT SUM(t.total) AS sum_of_totals, AVG(t.total - av.avg_total) AS avg_excess FROM t CROSS JOIN av WHERE t.total > av.avg_total
